Author: Shayah
Text: $AIP The market fundamentally misprices $AIP because it values it like a legacy software vendor rather than an asymmetric IP compounder. Monolithic silicon scaling has hit a physical wall, making heterogeneous chiplets the industry standard; the primary bottleneck is no longer raw compute density, but die-to-die latency and on-chip routing where OEMs cannot afford to reinvent NoC architecture and safety standards from scratch. While public markets fixate on near-term design licensing revenue, they miss the structural 3–5 year lag before those custom ASICs reach mass foundry tape-out and unlock high-margin production royalties. With an 85%+ gross margin profile and largely fixed R&D overhead, those compounding royalty streams drop straight through to Free Cash Flow—turning $AIP into the essential toll booth on the custom silicon megatrend without having to bet on which chipmaker wins.
